name: config_resource_update

collection.note: the core collection: an omitted or empty value means core, and the Tool sends collection=core on every Gateway read and write it makes; any other value fails with invalid_argument before anything is dispatched (D30 owner ruling 5)

targetId.collection: the core collection only: every read and every write names collection=core (the reads and the DELETE route as a query parameter, a change item as the field its documented request schema declares), so a Target is <resourceType>/<name> in that collection; a caller-supplied collection is accepted only when it is core, and any other value fails with invalid_argument before anything is dispatched (D30 owner ruling 5)
targetId.denialCodeSource: D30 §7, Tool-scoped; the Phase 3 machinery keeps operation_disabled

requestSchemaValidation.schema: the resource type's documented PUT request-body item schema, bundled into a self-contained JSON Schema (internal $refs hoisted to $defs) at capability refresh time
requestSchemaValidation.appliesTo: the complete change item, before dispatch
requestSchemaValidation.unavailableDisposition: a documented update route without a usable request schema exposes no update route, so the Tool refuses the resource type with unsupported_capability
requestSchemaValidation.dependency: jsonschema (already in uv.lock via fastmcp's OpenAPI server extra)
requestSchemaValidation.snapshotImmutability: the schema is deeply immutable inside the D04 snapshot (mappings are read-only views, arrays are tuples), so a holder of the snapshot cannot change the rules a later write is validated against
requestSchemaValidation.referenceBundling: internal $refs are hoisted into $defs once per target; every occurrence keeps its own sibling keywords (a later occurrence must not lose a constraint the earlier one did not carry)

changeItem: name is included when the documented item schema declares it; a singleton's change item carries only signature plus the supplied fields

rejectionPolicy.rule: D30 §2: an explicit Gateway rejection is the result of the attempt — a 4xx (including 409) or a 2xx carrying success=false with a problem. It is mapped to conflict for a signature mismatch, and no read-back may turn it into a success: a resource showing the requested values may have been changed by another writer.
verificationMaySucceedWhen: the Gateway claimed success (2xx with no refusal)
the dispatch was genuinely ambiguous (possibly sent with no response, or 5xx) and the change is attributable to this call
rejectionPolicy.ambiguousAttribution: a competing writer cannot be ruled out for an ambiguous dispatch, so a read-back that merely matches the requested values is outcome_unknown, never a success; a read-back still showing the pre-state is not_applied

verification: bounded re-read of the changed resource, reported as Observed state and used for the outcomes above
